expected.summary: Eighty minutes before the anchor chronyd on node ip-10-0-7-42.ec2.internal was OOM-killed and not restarted, so the node's clock stopped being synchronised and began running fast by about 4.5 seconds a minute. payment signs every charge to payments.example.com with a request timestamp, and the provider rejects requests more than 300 seconds off its own clock. Two of six payment pods, payment-2 and payment-4, run on that node. From about fifty minutes before the anchor the provider's replies to them carried a Warning header about the growing skew, and about thirteen minutes before the anchor the skew passed 300 seconds: since then every charge from those two pods fails with 401 timestamp_out_of_tolerance, which payment returns to checkout as a 502 within about 130 ms. The other four payment pods charge the same provider without errors, and fraud-3, which shares the node, is healthy because fraud signs nothing. Failed checkouts are not charged. The 502s propagate through checkout, web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. Nothing shipped and no version changed. The provider's scheduled maintenance notice for its payouts API (MNT-7731), posted sixteen minutes before the anchor, is a red herring: card charges from the four healthy pods succeed throughout, and the rejections name the request timestamp.
contributingFactors: chronyd dying on node ip-10-0-7-42 and staying down, so the node's clock drifted
the payment provider rejecting signed requests more than 300 seconds off its clock
no alert on clock synchronisation, so an hour of drift went unnoticed

criteria.description: Does the brief name clock skew on node ip-10-0-7-42, after chronyd died, making the provider reject the signed charges of the two payment pods on that node, with the checkout failures reaching edge-gateway? 5 = the node, both pods, the timestamp rejection and the victim chain. Blaming the provider or its maintenance scores 1; naming the two pods without the clock scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in the 401 timestamp_out_of_tolerance errors giving the skew, failures grouped by k8s.pod.name on payment-2 and payment-4, the chronyd log on the node, and the provider Warning headers that grew for half an hour before the failures? Cap at 3 unless it explains why the failures began over an hour after chronyd stopped.

Does it dismiss the provider maintenance notice with evidence (four pods charge fine against the same provider), note fraud-3 on the same node is healthy, avoid inventing a deploy, and avoid blaming checkout or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
